questions.q: Calculate the closing balance of single column cash book. Use the method 'Single Column Cash Book'. Work with: opening_cash = 75, total_cash_payments = 18, total_cash_receipts = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of closing_cash.

Find the cash in hand at the end of the month. Use the method 'Single Column Cash Book'. Work with: opening_cash = 60, total_cash_payments = 6, total_cash_receipts = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of closing_cash.
Explain in your own words what 'Single Column Cash Book' refers to.
questions.a: A primary financial record containing a single amount column on each side that documents all incoming and outgoing cash chronologically.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Single Column Cash Book'.
questions.a: Cash receipts are recorded on the debit side and cash payments on the credit side.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Single Column Cash Book', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Double Column Cash Book and Bank Balance

questions.q: Calculate closing bank balance in double column cash book. Use the method 'Double Column Cash Book and Bank Balance'. Work with: opening_bank = 8, total_bank_deposits = 25, total_bank_withdrawals = 30. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of closing_bank.

Find the bank balance c/d after recording deposits and payments. Use the method 'Double Column Cash Book and Bank Balance'. Work with: opening_bank = 4, total_bank_deposits = 240, total_bank_withdrawals = 45. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of closing_bank.
Explain in your own words what 'Double Column Cash Book and Bank Balance' refers to.
questions.a: A subsidiary book equipped with distinct cash and bank columns on both debit and credit sides to register physical cash and banking activities simultaneously.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Double Column Cash Book and Bank Balance'.
questions.a: Contra entries record mutual fund movements between cash and bank on both sides of the book.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Double Column Cash Book and Bank Balance', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System

questions.q: Calculate petty cash balance in hand at the end of the period. Use the method 'Petty Cash Book and Imprest System'. Work with: conveyance = 100, imprest_amount = 80000, miscellaneous = 360, postage = 1500, stationery = 80. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of closing_petty_balance.

Find the reimbursement amount needed under imprest system. Use the method 'Petty Cash Book and Imprest System'. Work with: conveyance = 45, imprest_amount = 20000, miscellaneous = 6, postage = 150, stationery = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of closing_petty_balance.
Explain in your own words what 'Petty Cash Book and Imprest System' refers to.
questions.a: A secondary ledger maintained by a petty cashier to account for frequent low-value disbursements funded by a predetermined float called the imprest.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Petty Cash Book and Imprest System'.
questions.a: The head cashier reimburses the exact sum of verified small expenditures to restore the original imprest float.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Petty Cash Book and Imprest System', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate net amount to be entered in purchases book. Use the method 'Purchases Journal and Trade Discount'. Work with: gross_amount = 5000, trade_discount_rate = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_purchases.

Find the total of purchases journal after trade discount. Use the method 'Purchases Journal and Trade Discount'. Work with: gross_amount = 2500, trade_discount_rate = 10. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_purchases.
Explain in your own words what 'Purchases Journal and Trade Discount' refers to.
questions.a: A dedicated subsidiary journal used exclusively to chronicle credit purchases of trading merchandise at net invoice price.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Purchases Journal and Trade Discount'.
questions.a: Only credit purchases of goods meant for resale are entered, excluding cash purchases and asset purchases.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Purchases Journal and Trade Discount', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the net value of goods returned to supplier. Use the method 'Purchases Return Journal'. Work with: gross_return_amount = 8000, trade_discount_rate = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_return_amount.

Find the amount to be recorded in purchases return book. Use the method 'Purchases Return Journal'. Work with: gross_return_amount = 20000, trade_discount_rate = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_return_amount.
Explain in your own words what 'Purchases Return Journal' refers to.
questions.a: A special daybook that records items of trading goods returned to suppliers along with debit note references.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Purchases Return Journal'.
questions.a: Supported by debit notes issued to creditors for defective or non-compliant merchandise returned.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Purchases Return Journal', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate net sales to be entered in the sales book. Use the method 'Sales Journal'. Work with: gross_sales_amount = 120000, trade_discount_rate = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_sales.

Find the total credit sales value after trade discount. Use the method 'Sales Journal'. Work with: gross_sales_amount = 2500, trade_discount_rate = 15. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_sales.
Explain in your own words what 'Sales Journal' refers to.
questions.a: A subsidiary record maintained to log all credit sales of merchandise to customers based on outgoing sales invoices.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sales Journal'.
questions.a: Cash sales and sales of non-inventory assets are omitted from the sales journal.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Sales Journal', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the net value of sales return. Use the method 'Sales Return Journal'. Work with: gross_sales_return = 120000, trade_discount_rate = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_sales_return.

Find the amount to be recorded in sales return book. Use the method 'Sales Return Journal'. Work with: gross_sales_return = 20000, trade_discount_rate = 8. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of net_sales_return.
Explain in your own words what 'Sales Return Journal' refers to.
questions.a: A designated daybook used to record returns of goods previously sold on credit, supported by credit notes issued to customers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sales Return Journal'.
questions.a: A credit note is issued to the customer acknowledging the reduction in their payable balance.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Sales Return Journal', in plain ASCII form.
Using the method 'Journal Proper Entries Classification', work with: total_journal_credit = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_journal_debit.
Take the relation taught for 'Journal Proper Entries Classification' and work with: total_journal_credit = 4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_journal_debit.
Explain in your own words what 'Journal Proper Entries Classification' refers to.
questions.a: A residual book of original entry utilized for transactions that cannot be accommodated within any of the specialized subsidiary journals.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Journal Proper Entries Classification'.
questions.a: Records opening, adjustment, rectification, transfer, and miscellaneous non-cash or non-trading entries.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Journal Proper Entries Classification', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the balance of ledger account. Use the method 'Balancing of Ledger Accounts'. Work with: total_credit = 400, total_debit = 500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of account_balance.

Find the balance c/d in ledger account. Use the method 'Balancing of Ledger Accounts'. Work with: total_credit = 240, total_debit = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of account_balance.
Explain in your own words what 'Balancing of Ledger Accounts' refers to.
questions.a: The periodic accounting routine of computing the total difference between debit and credit sides of an account to determine its net closing balance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Balancing of Ledger Accounts'.
questions.a: A debit balance arises when debit total exceeds credit total; a credit balance occurs when credit exceeds debit.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Balancing of Ledger Accounts', in plain ASCII form.
